newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Feb 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Feb 19.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- China denied that paramount leader Deng Xiaoping's health had deteriorated. But "reliable sources" said Deng did suffer a cerebral haemorrhage during Chinese New Year.
-- Concerns over the health of Chinese patriarch Deng Xiaoping rocked the Hong Kong stock market.

-- SING TAO DAILY -- Chinese experts who had experienced China's past political turmoils were not optimistic towards the future after Deng died, saying the contradictions between different political forces could not be under-estimated.

-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- Chief executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa said he was confident that his choices for the top officials of the future Hong Kong government would be endorsed by Beijing, who would issue appointment letters to the new officials.
-- Hong Kong young people were getting in to raves in recent months, dancing crazily for hours through the night. Many international DJs had been invited to host such rave parties.

-- WEN WEI PO --To celebrate Hong Kong's handover, 97 top Chinese calligraphers will write the Basic Law, the territory's future constitution, in different calligraphic styles. Their work will form a giant scroll 150-metres long and 1 metre wide.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- London's first Chinese L-share, Beijing Datang Power Generation, was expected to begin trading in London and Hong Kong on March 24. Sources said Datang's sponsors would begin a roadshow next Wednesday.
-- China was considering restricting foreign investment in textiles, garments and other sectors where domestic production capacity was excessive.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Chief executive-designate Tung hinted that he was considering making the head of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority report directly him rather than to the Financial Secretary's office.
